exposure: Clinical care aspects in cesarean delivery
outcome: Patient priorities in cesarean delivery anesthesia experience
Patient perspectives on cesarean delivery care
Provider perspectives on cesarean delivery care
Themes related to patient and provider attitudes and beliefs
cohort: The cohort included patients hospitalized within 72 hours of a term gestation cesarean delivery and clinical care providers with at least 3 years of experience providing regular care to cesarean delivery patients.
finding: Both patients and providers desire effective pain management, psychological well-being, and clear communication during cesarean delivery, with patients prioritizing relationships and trust, and clinicians focusing on clinical complexities and physical treatments.
mod_finding: The study identified five major themes each for patient and provider attitudes regarding the cesarean delivery experience, covering communication, emotional support, pain management, acceptability of therapies, stigma, clinical complexities, and psychological well-being.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from patients within 72 hours of their cesarean delivery while still in the hospital.
